_comment: Web-verified written form of the Dato'/Datuk and Seri/Sri honorific, one entry per person,
read by check_honorifics.py. The spelling follows the person's OWN official page (Parliament,
PMO, a ministry or state site), never the corpus's majority. Dato' and Datuk, Seri and Sri,
are pronounced the same, so the video cannot decide them. The GRADE (Tun, Tan Sri, Datuk
Seri, Datuk) is spoken, and the checker never changes it: a speaker's slip stays verbatim
(owner's rule, 2026-10-04). `held` records the grade the person held on 2026-10 so a
mismatch is reported for the owner to read, not fixed.
forms: DSERI = the Seri/Sri grade, DATUK = the bare Datuk/Dato' grade.

Rule (says.com/my/lifestyle/dato-datuk-seri-difference, owner 2026-10-04): Dato' and Dato' Seri come from the nine state rulers, Dato' Sri ONLY from the Sultan of Pahang; Datuk and Datuk Seri come from the Agong or a governor (Melaka, Sabah, Sarawak). There is no 'Datuk Sri'.
